title: Analytic local ideal of a smooth closed algebraic subvariety
statement: Let $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be a closed immersion of smooth separated finite-type schemes over $\mathbf C$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use the analytifications and their ringed-space maps of [lem-sfb-smooth-analytification-cotangent]. For $x\in X^{\mathrm{an}}$, put $y=i^{\mathrm{an}}(x)$, $x_0=\pi_X(x)$ and $y_0=i(x_0)=\pi_Y(y)$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y_0}$, $R=\mathcal O_{X,x_0}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Y^{\mathrm{an}},y}$ and $D=\mathcal O_{X^{\mathrm{an}},x}$, where stalks are germs of sections over open neighbourhoods [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Let $I=\ker(i^\sharp_{x_0}:A\to R)$, and let $IB$ denote the ideal of $B$ generated by the images of all elements of $I$ under the analytification homomorphism $A\to B$. The analytic restriction homomorphism $B\to D$ is surjective with kernel exactly $IB$; hence its induced $B$-algebra homomorphism $B/IB\to D$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: WANTED locally: Serre, Géométrie algébrique et géométrie analytique, §6 Proposition 4, printed pp.10–11 (the analytic ideal is generated by the algebraic ideal), and its use in §10 Proposition 11, printed p.18. Read online https://www.numdam.org/article/AIF_1956__6__1_0.pdf.

proof.text: Work at the given complex points. By the analytification theorem, $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ and $Y^{\mathrm{an}}$ are complex manifolds near $x,y$, of dimensions $d,n$, and $i^{\mathrm{an}}$ is a holomorphic embedding. The maps from algebraic germs send a regular function to that same holomorphic germ, so restriction commutes with these maps. In particular every $f\in I$ maps to zero in $D$, giving $IB\subseteq\ker(B\to D)$. The residue fields at $x_0,y_0$ are canonically $\mathbf C$: on an affine neighbourhood evaluation at the complex point is a surjective $\mathbf C$-algebra map to $\mathbf C$, with kernel its maximal ideal. For an algebraic module $E$ on $T\in\{X,Y\}$ and $z\in T^{\mathrm{an}}$, the tensor-stalk isomorphism over the ringed space $(T^{\mathrm{an}},\pi_T^{-1}\mathcal O_T)$ and the inverse-image stalk isomorphism give $(E^{\mathrm{an}})_z=\mathcal O_{T^{\mathrm{an}},z}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{T,\pi_T(z)}}E_{\pi_T(z)}$, so $(E^{\mathrm{an}})_z\otimes\mathbf C=E_{\pi_T(z)}\otimes\mathbf C$; in a chart the holomorphic one-forms are free on the coordinate differentials, so $\Omega^1_{T^{\mathrm{an}},z}\otimes\mathbf C=T_z^*T^{\mathrm{an}}$. Hence the cotangent comparison, evaluated at the point, identifies the algebraic cotangent fibres with $T_x^*X^{\mathrm{an}}$ and $T_y^*Y^{\mathrm{an}}$, sending $df$ to the differential of the holomorphic germ. This identification commutes with restriction: both maps send $df$ to $d(i^*f)$, and differentials of regular functions generate the algebraic differential sheaf.

source.place: WANTED locally: Serre §2 no.6 Proposition 4, printed pp.10–11, and §3 no.10 Proposition 11, printed p.18. Agent smooth-coordinate proof, rather than Serre's general completion/analytic-Nullstellensatz proof; online source read at https://www.numdam.org/article/AIF_1956__6__1_0.pdf.

proof.text: Apply the conormal fibre sequence over $\mathbf C$ to the given closed immersion, whose source is smooth. Under the identifications in Step 1 it states that the kernel of $T_y^*Y^{\mathrm{an}}\to T_x^*X^{\mathrm{an}}$ is spanned by $df(y)$ for $f\in I$, and that this map is surjective. Thus $n\geq d$; put $r=n-d$ and choose $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in I$ whose differentials form a basis of that kernel. Indeed the image of $(I/I^2)\otimes\mathbf C$ is spanned by the images of the pure classes $[f]\otimes1$, so ordinary finite-dimensional basis selection chooses such actual elements of $I$. Their analytic representatives vanish on $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ on a common neighbourhood of $x$.

source.place: Tag 06AA, lemma-differentials-relative-immersion-smooth, lines 7429–7454; the cited node includes the residue-field fibre and the generator formula.

proof.text: Choose holomorphic coordinates $q$ on $Y^{\mathrm{an}}$ centred at $y$. Complete $df_1(y),\ldots,df_r(y)$ to a basis of $T_y^*Y^{\mathrm{an}}$ by constant linear combinations $dt_1,\ldots,dt_d$ of the $dq_j$, and take $t_j(y)=0$. The map $F=(f_1^{\mathrm{an}},\ldots,f_r^{\mathrm{an}},t_1,\ldots,t_d)$ is holomorphic by the function-operations lemma. Its derivative at $y$ is invertible by this basis choice and the tuple derivative formula. The inverse toolkit therefore gives a biholomorphic germ $F:(Y^{\mathrm{an}},y)\to(\mathbf C^r\times\mathbf C^d,0)$. The images of $dt_j$ form a basis of $T_x^*X^{\mathrm{an}}$, so the same theorem on the source makes $t\circ i^{\mathrm{an}}$ a biholomorphic germ $(X^{\mathrm{an}},x)\to(\mathbf C^d,0)$. This also applies to zero-dimensional vector spaces.

proof.text: In these germs the immersion is exactly $t\mapsto(0,t)$: its normal coordinates vanish by Step 2 and its remaining coordinates equal $t$ by construction. This is also an equality on neighbourhoods. Let $s$ be the local inverse of $t\circ i^{\mathrm{an}}$. Shrink its domain so that $i^{\mathrm{an}}s(t)$ lies in the source of the ambient inverse $F^{-1}$; then $F(i^{\mathrm{an}}s(t))=(0,t)$ implies $i^{\mathrm{an}}s(t)=F^{-1}(0,t)$. Because $i^{\mathrm{an}}$ is a topological embedding, an ambient neighbourhood can be chosen whose inverse image is in this source chart. After shrinking to a product neighbourhood in the $F$-coordinates, its intersection with the image is therefore precisely the coordinate slice $z=0$.

source.place: WANTED locally: Serre §2 no.6 Proposition 4, printed pp.10–11, and §3 no.10 Proposition 11, printed p.18. Agent smooth-coordinate proof, rather than Serre's general completion/analytic-Nullstellensatz proof; online source read at https://www.numdam.org/article/AIF_1956__6__1_0.pdf.

proof.text: For a germ $h\in D$, use the source coordinate $t$ to write it as a holomorphic germ $h_0(t)$. Its extension $h_0(t)$ independent of $z$, composed with $F$, is a holomorphic germ in $B$ by the function-operations lemma, and restricts to $h$. Hence $B\to D$ is surjective. If $b\in B$ restricts to zero, write $H=b\circ F^{-1}$. Then $H(0,t)=0$ as a germ by Step 4. Holomorphic coordinate division gives $H=\sum_{j=1}^r z_jH_j$ with each $H_j$ jointly holomorphic. Composing with $F$ gives $b=\sum_j f_j^{\mathrm{an}}(H_j\circ F)\in IB$. Along with Step 1 this proves $\ker(B\to D)=IB$.

source.place: WANTED locally: Serre §2 no.6 Proposition 4, printed pp.10–11, and §3 no.10 Proposition 11, printed p.18. Agent smooth-coordinate proof, rather than Serre's general completion/analytic-Nullstellensatz proof; online source read at https://www.numdam.org/article/AIF_1956__6__1_0.pdf.

proof.text: The homomorphism $\bar\rho:B/IB\to D$, $[b]\mapsto\rho(b)$, is well-defined because $IB$ is its kernel. It is surjective since $\rho$ is. If $\bar\rho([b])=0$, then $b\in IB$, so $[b]=0$; it is injective. Its inverse is the unique preimage map, which preserves addition, multiplication and $1$ by injectivity. Both maps respect the $B$-action by the defining formula, so this is the claimed $B$-algebra isomorphism. If $r=0$ the division formula gives zero kernel; if $d=0$ extension is extension of constants; if $X$ is empty there is no point to check.

lean.statement: theorem exists_analyticClosedIdealLocalQuotient {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℂ))) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℂ))) [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [Smooth f] [IsSeparated g] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [QuasiCompact g] [Smooth g] (D : Data f) (E : Data g) (i : Over.mk f ⟶ Over.mk g) [IsClosedImmersion i.left] : ∃ (j : D.space ⟶ E.space) (hπ : ∀ x : D.space, i.left (D.pi.hom.base x) = E.pi.hom.base (j.hom.base x)), (∀ x : D.space, j.hom.base x = mapPoints D E i x) ∧ (∀ (U : Opens E.space) (a : E.space.presheaf.obj (op U)) (x : (Opens.map j.hom.base).obj U), D.functions.eval _ (j.hom.c.app (op U) a) x = E.functions.eval U a ⟨j.hom.base x.val, x.property⟩) ∧ ∀ x : D.space, Function.Surjective (j.hom.stalkMap x).hom ∧ RingHom.ker (j.hom.stalkMap x).hom = closedIdeal D E i j hπ x ∧ ∃ e : (E.space.presheaf.stalk (j.hom.base x)) ⧸ closedIdeal D E i j hπ x ≃+* D.space.presheaf.stalk x, ∀ b : E.space.presheaf.stalk (j.hom.base x), e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (closedIdeal D E i j hπ x) b) = j.hom.stalkMap x b
